sources.title: Akhil Mathew, Sperner’s Lemma, Brouwer’s Fixed-Point Theorem, and the Subdivision of Squares into Triangles
sources.actual_text_read: Physical/printed pages1-3, sections1-2 only; the section3 start on page3 is excluded from use.
sources.supported_scope: Two-dimensional marked-edge parity and the deficit-label/compactness route to Brouwer in dimension2.
proof_limits: The source explicitly proves Brouwer only for n=2. Our arbitrary-dimensional parity induction, compatible barycentric subdivisions, mesh contraction and projection extension are supplied independently.
Page2 says the non-full case is odd, immediately contradicted by its own tau=2 example; use even.
No nesting of selected full simplices is needed or claimed; a compact subsequence plus vanishing mesh supplies the limit.
No valuation or Monsky result is used.

sources.title: Omer Tamuz, General Equilibrium Theory, Lecture Notes
sources.version: Cover says2021; retrieval header Last-Modified7April2026 is retained as metadata, not an invented publication date.
sources.actual_text_read: Physical/printed pages1,4-7,13-17: preferences and convexity versus convexity-star, prices/choice, production support, Walras accounting/free disposal, full compactification page14, Kakutani/Debreu statements, existence and the compact exchange argument.
sources.supported_scope: Correspondence/price-auction architecture and private ownership accounting; distinctions between convex preferences and the stronger strict-improvement mixture condition.
proof_limits: Kakutani is stated, not proved; our complete proof derives it from the proved finite-dimensional Brouwer result.
The source defines UHC through sequential closed graph. Our chapter defines the open-neighborhood notion and proves equivalence with closed graph only with compact range and closed values.

The general page14 cone-enlargement compactification is not adopted. Passing to a closed conical hull need not preserve the original no-free-production hypothesis: (-epsilon^2,epsilon) can scale to(-epsilon,1) and converge to(0,1). Our theorem uses an explicit compact generator instead.
No global LNS is inferred on an entire bounded box from strict monotonicity at its maximal corner. Budget exhaustion is proved only after the fixed allocation is strictly below the cap.
Our cap removal uses convex preferences, strict cheaper scaling and a coordinate improvement; it does not import convexity-star or the source general existence theorem.

sources.title: Scott Condie, Advanced Microeconomic Theory Class Notes, Chapter7: The Existence of General Equilibrium
sources.version: Mutable author-hosted HTML retrieved9October2026; header modification date is not a publication date.
sources.actual_text_read: Complete web-rendered chapter7 sections7.1-7.2, Propositions7.1-7.3 and all five proof steps, including boundary correspondence equation7.1. Local raw HTML retained.
sources.supported_scope: Normalized prices, full excess-demand conditions, Walras-law and price-maximizer route, and why boundary behavior requires proof.
proof_limits: Its interior excess-demand/boundary-blowup route is context, not the theorem imported here; our economic proof derives every correspondence property from individual assumptions and compact generators.
No aggregate-wealth bound is silently substituted for positive wealth for each household. Our assumptions give omega_i strictly positive individually.
